reason: E2 mentions substrate heating as a strategy to mitigate thermal stresses and hot cracking in HEAs, supporting the general premise. However, no cited evidence directly tests preheating on AlCrFeNiSi or quantifies its effect on segregation, residual stress, and mechanical integrity for this alloy. E1 and E3 address different materials (AlFeCoCrNi2.1 and H13 tool steel) and post-process heat treatment or in-situ tempering, not substrate preheating during AM of AlCrFeNiSi. Thus, the specific claims for this alloy lack direct support.
premises: Substrate preheating reduces thermal gradients and cooling rates in AM
Reduced cooling rates limit compositional segregation
Reduced cooling rates lower residual stresses
Lower segregation and residual stress improve mechanical integrity
These mechanisms apply to AlCrFeNiSi HEA
